questions.q:
Please read the passage and answer the questions that follow. (Q. No. 1 to 7)
Trees are among the most valuable resources on Earth. They play a vital role in maintaining ecological balance and supporting life. One of the most important functions of trees is producing oxygen, which living organisms need to breathe. At the same time, trees absorb carbon dioxide from the atmosphere, helping reduce air pollution and regulate the climate. Because of this ability, forests are often called the “lungs of the planet”.
Apart from improving air quality, trees also help conserve water and prevent soil erosion. Their roots hold the soil firmly and reduce the chances of floods and landslides. Trees provide shelter, food, and breeding grounds for many birds and animals, making them essential for biodiversity. In urban areas, trees provide shade, reduce heat, and make the environment more pleasant.
Unfortunately, large numbers of trees are cut down every year for construction and industrial activities. This deforestation harms wildlife and contributes to climate change. Therefore, planting and protecting trees has become an important responsibility for people everywhere. Governments, schools, and communities often organize tree-planting campaigns to raise awareness about environmental protection.
If more trees are planted and preserved, the Earth can remain a healthier and more beautiful place for future generations.
Why are forests called the “lungs of the planet”?
Select the most appropriate option.
o: They conserve water and prevent soil erosion.
They absorb oxygen and produce carbon dioxide.
They produce oxygen and absorb carbon dioxide.
They drain out toxic minerals from the food chain.
